fault_injection.description: The explicit missing-column validation was removed from starter_repo/plot_data.py so pandas raises KeyError instead of the required ValueError.
fault_injection.expected_initial_result: The first test node records pytest exit code 1 and routes to fix.
fault_injection.expected_recovery: The fix node restores correct validation in the current fixture, and the next test routes to END.

task.title: Raise ValueError for missing CSV columns
task.description: Improve starter_repo.plot_data.read_csv_data while preserving the existing plotting command-line interface and unrelated behavior.
requirements: Preserve the current behavior when both requested columns exist.
If x_col or y_col is missing from the CSV data, raise ValueError instead of allowing pandas to raise KeyError.
The ValueError message must identify the missing column name or names.
Add pytest tests under tests/ for valid columns, a missing x column, and a missing y column.
Do not change the command-line interface or unrelated plotting behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Valid input still returns the selected x and y values.
A missing requested column raises ValueError containing its name.

plan.content: Validate both requested column names immediately after reading the CSV and before DataFrame indexing. Collect missing names in request order without duplicates, raise a descriptive ValueError containing every missing name, preserve the successful return path, and leave plotting and CLI behavior unchanged.
plan.source: seeded from the accepted run-002 implementation context

code.content: The accepted implementation added an ordered missing_columns list in read_csv_data(), populated it from (x_col, y_col) when names were absent from df.columns, raised ValueError with the joined missing names when the list was non-empty, and otherwise returned df[x_col].tolist(), df[y_col].tolist(). The run-003 fault injection removed that validation block from the current fixture.
